newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan finmin-GDP to fall to 5.2 percent in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Jordan finmin-GDP to fall to 5.2 percent in 1996.

text.p: Jordan's economy is forecast to grow at just 5.2 percent in 1996, down from 6.9 percent in 1995, the finance minister said on Wednesday.
"The preliminary results show that the GDP will grow this year at 5.2 percent in constant prices against 6.9 percent in 1995," Marwan Awad told parliament in a speech on the 1997 draft budget.
The government is setting a target of 6.5 percent GDP growth in 1997 with new economic legislation that should boost the investment climate and draw more domestic and foreign investments, Awad said.

While Jordan's main hard currency earners -- the potash and posphates industries -- were expected to grow by around 10 percent in 1996, retail and wholesale trade, transport and communications were estimated to grow at six percent, Awad said.

Jordan announced projected state spending in 1997 will total 1.916 billion dinars -- an 11 percent rise from 1996 adjusted budget figures -- while the deficit minus foreign aid would reach 3.9 percent of GDP, or 225 million dinars.
The budget deficit is expected to be a readjusted 237 million dinars in 1996, or 4.6 percent of GDP.
